blocks.en: A couple of years ago a friend of mine, a newspaper editor, was fire watching with some factory workers. They fell to talking about his newspaper, which most of them read and approved of, but when he asked them what they thought of the literary section, the answer he got was: "You don't suppose we read that stuff, do you? Why, half the time you're talking about books that cost twelve and sixpence! Chaps like us couldn't spend twelve and sixpence on a book." These, he said, were men who thought nothing of spending several pounds on a day trip to Blackpool.
blocks.zh: 几年前，我的一位朋友，一名报社编辑，正和一些工厂工人一起进行火情巡查。他们聊起了他的报纸，那家报纸他们大多都读，也颇为认可。可当他问起大家对文学版的看法时，得到的回答却是：“您不会真以为我们会看那些东西吧？哎呀，你们有一半时间都在谈那些要一镑二先令的书呢！像我们这种人哪舍得在一本上花一镑二先令。”他说，这些人为了去布莱克浦玩一天，花上几英镑也毫不在意。

blocks.en: This idea that the buying, or even the reading, of books is an expensive hobby and beyond the reach of the average person is so widespread that it deserves some detailed examination. Exactly what reading costs, reckoned in terms of pence per hour, is difficult to estimate, but I have made a start by inventorying my own books and adding up their total price. After allowing for various other expenses, I can make a fairly good guess at my expenditure over the last fifteen years.
blocks.zh: 认为购买书籍，甚至阅读书籍，都是一种昂贵的爱好，普通人难以负担的观点如此普遍，以至于值得我们对其进行深入探讨。究竟阅读的成本——以每小时几便士来衡量——很难估算，但我已着手清点自己的藏书，并将其总价相加。在扣除各项其他开支后，我大致可以估算出过去十五年的支出情况。

blocks.en: The books that I have counted and priced are the ones I have here, in my flat. I have about an equal number stored in another place, so that I shall double the final figure in order to arrive at the complete amount. I have not counted oddments such as proof copies, defaced volumes, cheap paper-covered editions, pamphlets, or magazines, unless bound up into book form. Nor have I counted the kind of junky books-old school text-books and so forth—that accumulate in the bottoms of cupboards. I have counted only those books which I have acquired voluntarily, or else would have acquired voluntarily, and which I intend to keep. In this category I find that I have 442 books, acquired in the following ways:
blocks.zh: 我已经清点并定价的书，就放在我家公寓里。我在另一个地方也存有大致相同数量的物品，因此我将把最终数字翻倍，以得出总数。我并未统计诸如校样、污损本、廉价纸面装订本、小册子或杂志等零散出版物，除非它们已被装订成书。我也没有统计那些堆在橱柜底部的各类杂物——旧课本之类的东西。我只统计了那些我自愿获得、或者本会自愿获得，并且打算留存的书籍。在这一类别中，我发现我共有442本书，它们的获取途径如下：

blocks.en: Now as to the method of pricing. Those books that I have bought I have listed at their full price, as closely as I can determine it. I have also listed at their full price the books that have been given to me, and those that I have temporarily borrowed, or borrowed and kept. This is because book-giving, book-borrowing and book stealing more or less even out. I possess books that do not strictly speaking belong to me, but many other people also have books of mine: so that the books I have not paid for can be taken as balancing others which I have paid for but no longer possess. On the other hand I have listed the review and complimentary copies at half-price. That is about what I would have paid for them second-hand, and they are mostly books that I would only have bought second-hand, if at all. For the prices I have sometimes had to rely on guesswork, but my figures will not be far out. The costs were as follows:
blocks.zh: 至于定价方法。我已将所购书籍按其全价列出，尽可能准确地依据我所能确定的价格。我也按原价列出了那些赠予我的书籍，以及那些我暂时借阅或借阅后留用的书籍。这是因为赠书、借书与偷书在某种程度上相互抵消。我拥有的一些书严格说来并不属于我，但也有许多我的书被他人持有：这样一来，那些我没有付费购买的书籍便可以被视为与我曾付费购得却已不再拥有的书籍相互抵消。另一方面，我已将书评和赠阅本以半价列出。那差不多就是我会为它们支付的二手价，而且这些书大多是我就算买也只会买二手的。至于价格，我有时不得不凭猜测来估算，但我的数据应该不会相差太远。费用如下：

£   s.   d.
Bought                    36    9    0
Gifts                     10   10    0
Review copies, etc        25   11    9
Borrowed and not returned  4   16    9
On loan                    3   10    0
Shelves                    2    0    0
Total                     82   17    6

Adding the other batch of books that I have elsewhere, it seems that I possess altogether nearly 900 books, at a cost of £165 15s. This is the accumulation of about fifteen years—actually more, since some of these books date from my childhood: but call it fifteen years. This works out at £11 1s. a year, but there are other charges that must be added in order to estimate my full reading expenses. The biggest will be for newspapers and periodicals, and for this I think £8 a year would be a reasonable figure. Eight pounds a year covers the cost of two daily papers, one evening paper, two Sunday papers, one weekly review and one or two monthly magazines. This brings the figure up to £19 1s., but to arrive at the grand total one has to make a guess. Obviously one often spends money on books without afterwards having anything to show for it. There are library subscriptions, and there are also the books, chiefly Penguins and other cheap editions, which one buys and then loses or throws away. However, on the basis of my other figures, it looks as though £6 a year would be quite enough to add for expenditure of this kind. So my total reading expenses over the past fifteen years have been in the neighbourhood of £25 a year.
blocks.zh: 加上我在其他地方拥有的另一批书，看来我总共拥有近900本书，165 15英镑。这是大约十五年的积累-实际上更多，因为其中一些书可以追溯到我的童年: 但称之为十五年。这相当于11英镑1先令。一年的费用，但还需要加上其他各项开支，才能估算出我全部的阅读支出。其中，报纸和期刊的补贴额度将最高，对此我认为每年8英镑是一个合理的数额。每年8英镑可支付两份日报，一份晚报，两份周日报纸，一份每周评论和一份或两份月刊的费用。这样一来，总额就达到了19英镑1先令，但要得出最终的总计，还得做个估算。显然，人们常常花钱买书，却事后一无所获。有图书馆订阅，也有书籍，主要是企鹅和其他廉价版本，人们购买然后丢失或扔掉。然而，根据我的其他数字，似乎每年6英镑足以增加这种支出。因此，过去十五年里，我的年度购书支出大约为25英镑。

blocks.en: Twenty-five pounds a year sounds quite a lot until you begin to measure it against other kinds of expenditure. It is nearly 9s. 9d. a week, and at present 9s. 9d. is the equivalent of about 83 cigarettes (Players): even before the war it would have bought you less than 200 cigarettes. With prices as they now are, I am spending far more on tobacco than I do on books. I smoke six ounces a week, at half-a-crown an ounce, making nearly £40 a year. Even before the war when the same tobacco cost 8d. an ounce, I was spending over £10 a year on it: and if I also averaged a pint of beer a day, at sixpence, these two items together will have cost me close on £20 a year. This was probably not much above the national average. In 1938 the people of this country spent nearly £10 per head per annum on alcohol and tobacco: however, 20 per cent of the population were children under fifteen and another 40 per cent were women, so that the average smoker and drinker must have been spending much more than £10. In 1944, the annual expenditure per head on these items was no less than £23. Allow for the women and children as before, and £40 is a reasonable individual figure. Forty pounds a year would just about pay for a packet of Woodbines every day and half a pint of mild six days a week—not a magnificent allowance. Of course, all prices are now inflated, including the price of books: still, it looks as though the cost of reading, even if you buy books instead of borrowing them and take in a fairly large number of periodicals, does not amount to more than the combined cost of smoking and drinking.
blocks.zh: 25英镑一年听起来相当多，直到你开始衡量它与其他种类的支出。快9点了。9天。一周，目前为9先令。9天。这相当于大约83支香烟（玩家）：即便在战前，这也只能买到不到200支香烟。以目前的物价水平，我在烟草上的花费远远超过了在书本上的支出。我每周抽六盎司烟，每盎司售价半克朗，一年下来差不多要花四十英镑。甚至在战争之前，同样的烟草售价为8便士。一盎司，我每年在这上面的花费超过10英镑: 如果我每天平均喝一品脱啤酒，六便士，这两项加在一起每年将使我损失近20英镑。这可能与全国平均水平相差无几。在1938，这个国家的人民每年在烟酒上的花费接近每人10英镑: 然而，人口的20% 是15岁以下的儿童，另外40% 是妇女，因此，吸烟者和饮酒者的平均花费必须超过10英镑。1944年，这些项目的年人均支出不少于23英镑。仍按先前的做法，为妇女和儿童预留名额，每人40英镑是合理的数额。每年40英镑几乎可以支付每天一包Woodbines的费用，每周六天半品脱温和的费用，这不是一个了不起的津贴。当然，现在所有的价格都被抬高了，包括书籍的价格: 尽管如此，看起来阅读的成本，即使你买书而不是借书，并接受相当大数量的期刊，也不会超过吸烟和喝酒。

blocks.en: It is difficult to establish any relationship between the price of books and the value one gets out of them. "Books" includes novels, poetry, text books, works of reference, sociological treatises and much else, and length and price do not correspond to one another, especially if one habitually buys books second-hand. You may spend ten shillings on a poem of 500 lines, and you may spend sixpence on a dictionary which you consult at odd moments over a period of twenty years. There are books that one reads over and over again, books that become part of the furniture of one's mind and alter one's whole attitude to life, books that one dips into but never reads through, books that one reads at a single sitting and forgets a week later: and the cost, in terms of money, may be the same in each case. But if one regards reading simply as a recreation, like going to the pictures, then it is possible to make a rough estimate of what it costs. If you read nothing but novels and "light" literature, and bought every book that you read, you would be spending-allowing eight shillings as the price of a book, and four hours as the time spent in reading it-two shillings an hour. This is about what it costs to sit in one of the more expensive seats in the cinema. If you concentrated on more serious books, and still bought everything that you read, your expenses would be about the same. The books would cost more but they would take longer to read. In either case you would still possess the books after you had read them, and they would be saleable at about a third of their purchase price. If you bought only second-hand books, your reading expenses would, of course, be much less: perhaps sixpence an hour would be a fair estimate. And on the other hand if you don't buy books, but merely borrow them from the lending library, reading costs you round about a halfpenny an hour: if you borrow them from the public library, it costs you next door to nothing.
blocks.zh: 很难在书籍的价格和人们从中获得的价值之间建立任何关系。“书籍” 包括小说，诗歌，教科书，参考书，社会学论文等，长度和价格彼此不对应，尤其是如果人们习惯性地购买二手书。你可以花十先令写一首500行的诗，你可以花六便士买一本字典，你可以在二十年的时间里偶尔查阅。有些书是一个人一遍又一遍地读的，有些书成为一个人心灵的家具的一部分，改变了一个人对生活的整体态度，有些书是一个人潜入但从不通读的，有些书是一个人坐着读了，一周后就忘记了。就金钱而言，在每种情况下可能都是相同的。但是，如果一个人认为阅读只是一种娱乐，就像去看照片一样，那么就有可能粗略估计它的成本。如果你只看小说和 “轻” 文学，买了你读的每一本书，你将花费 -- 允许八先令作为一本书的价格，和四个小时的时间花在阅读 -- 两个先令一小时。这是关于坐在电影院中较昂贵的座位之一的费用。如果您专注于更严肃的书籍，并且仍然购买您阅读的所有内容，那么您的支出将大致相同。这些书会花更多的钱，但要花更长的时间阅读。在任何一种情况下，你仍然会拥有这些书你读了他们，他们将出售大约三分之一的购买价格。如果你只买二手书，你的阅读费用当然会少得多: 也许每小时六便士是一个公平的估计。另一方面，如果您不买书，而只是从借书图书馆借书，那么阅读每小时要花费您大约半便士: 如果您从公共图书馆借书，那么隔壁的费用将一分钱不花。

blocks.en: I have said enough to show that reading is one of the cheaper recreations: after listening to the radio probably THE cheapest. Meanwhile, what is the actual amount that the British public spends on books? I cannot discover any figures, though no doubt they exist. But I do know that before the war this country was publishing annually about 15,000 books, which included reprints and school books. If as many as 10,000 copies of each book were sold—and even allowing for the school books, this is probably a high estimate-the average person was only buying, directly or indirectly, about three books a year. These three books taken together might cost £1, or probably less.
blocks.zh: 我已经说得足够多了，表明阅读是一种更便宜的娱乐方式: 听广播后可能是最便宜的。同时，英国公众在书籍上的实际花费是多少？我没有发现任何数字，尽管毫无疑问它们是存在的。但我确实知道，在战争之前，这个国家每年出版约15,000本书，其中包括重印本和学校书籍。如果每本书售出多达10,000册-甚至考虑到学校书籍，这可能是一个很高的估计-普通人每年只直接或间接购买大约三本书。这三本书加在一起可能要花1英镑，甚至更少。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: These figures are guesswork, and I should be interested if someone would correct them for me. But if my estimate is anywhere near right, it is not a proud record for a country which is nearly 100 per cent literate and where the ordinary man spends more on cigarettes than an Indian peasant has for his whole livelihood. And if our book consumption remains as low as it has been, at least let us admit that it is because reading is a less exciting pastime than going to the dogs, the pictures or the pub, and not because books, whether bought or borrowed, are too expensive.
blocks.zh: 这些数字是猜测，我应该感兴趣，如果有人能纠正他们对我。但是，如果我的估计接近正确的话，对于一个识字率接近100% 的国家来说，这不是一个值得骄傲的记录，在这个国家，普通人在香烟上的花费比印度农民的整个生计还多。如果我们的图书消费仍然像以前一样低，至少让我们承认，这是因为阅读是一种比去狗，图片或酒吧更不令人兴奋的消遣，而不是因为书，无论是买的还是借的，太贵了。
